exclusion_reason: Implemented but red because FIX-016 also measures jitter against a budget on a real running frame loop and the yield-not-spin property of the busy-wait under the async browser present path (requestAnimationFrame + the AudioWorklet clock), which does not run in this worktree — there is no live frame loop to pace yet. The pacer core exists generically in lib/clock.mjs over the one monotonic guest clock: createFramePacer resolves a frame ready at a guest time onto the next vertical-blank boundary at the declared refresh rate, counts presented frames, and reports the vblanks a stall skipped as dropped rather than absorbing them — speed follows the one clock, so it is host-throughput independent by construction.
promotion_trigger: Promote when cadence, speed independence, and the yield-not-spin property all hold on the fixture.
expected_failing_assertion: No live browser frame loop drives the pacer, so jitter against the budget and the yield-not-spin busy-wait cannot be measured.
active_gate_evidence: Tests prove the pacer syncs a frame to the next vblank boundary, counts presented frames, reports the dropped vblanks on a stall, and reads its present time from the one guest clock so cadence is host-independent; the clock keeps one monotonic source with clamped delta. The full suite stays green.
procedure: Run the frame fixture at the declared cadence.
Measure jitter against the budget and speed against host throughput change.
Assert the busy-wait call yields instead of spinning.
pass_criterion: Speed is host-independent and the wait yields.
